title: Mandarin Oriental Breaks Ground on Brickell Key
igCaption:
Mandarin Oriental and Swire Properties have broken ground on a new Brickell Key complex after presales topped $1.7 billion.
The old hotel opened in November 2000 and came down by implosion on April 12, 2026.
Would you live on Brickell Key when the new towers open?

Sources: CoStar, The Business Journals, Wikipedia: Mandarin Oriental, Miami, Wikipedia: Brickell Key, Wikipedia: Swire Properties

#Miami #Brickell #BrickellKey #MiamiRealEstate

scenes.text: Brickell Key just broke ground on a Mandarin Oriental project with more than one point seven billion dollars in presales.

Mandarin Oriental and Swire Properties broke ground on the new Brickell Key hotel and condo towers. Presales have already topped one point seven billion dollars before the replacement complex opens on the southern tip of the island.
scenes.caption: Mandarin Oriental and Swire Properties broke ground on the new Brickell Key hotel and condo towers. Presales have already topped $1.7B before the replacement complex opens on the southern tip of the island.

scenes.text: The old Mandarin Oriental opened in November 2000. It had 295 guestrooms, 31 suites with balconies and terraces, and 15,000 square feet of event space overlooking Biscayne Bay.
scenes.caption: The old Mandarin Oriental opened in November 2000. It had 295 guestrooms, 31 suites with balconies and terraces, and 15,000 sq ft of event space overlooking Biscayne Bay.

scenes.text: That building came down by implosion on April 12, 2026. It opened in 2000.
scenes.caption: That building came down by implosion on April 12, 2026. It opened in 2000.

scenes.text: The replacement plan calls for a 66-story tower and a 34-story tower. Together, they will contain 326 private residences and 121 hotel guest rooms, scheduled to open in 2030.
scenes.caption: The replacement plan calls for a 66-story tower and a 34-story tower. Together, they will contain 326 private residences and 121 hotel guest rooms, scheduled to open in 2030.

scenes.text: Brickell Key has Swire history built into it. Swire bought most of the island in the late 1970s, after Edward Claughton combined the islands into a 44-acre triangle-shaped tract in 1943.

scenes.text: Would you live on Brickell Key when this opens in 2030? Hard to keep track of the people you keep passing in a city that changes this fast, which is exactly where NEAR connects the face you saw to the name you never got.
